_meta: The coordinate system is positive X foreward (bow), positive Y upward, and positive Z to the right (starboard).

This file is 'CargoSub_main.json', and is the top level design file for CargoSub. Separate design files for large or complex subsystems will be explicitly named, with placeholders in this file, for organization. Controller functional requirements will be in json, but it is generally understood that they will be implemented as Lua scripts.

CargoSub.description: CargoSub is a large, conventionally shaped submarine with a large, central cargo bay. The cargo bay top and bottom hull sections are sealable custom doors/hatches opening over the full length and almost full width of the cargo bay. Oversized cargo can be loaded/unloaded through the top hatch while surfaced at ports. That cargo can be loaded/unloaded through the bottom hatch, on the seafloor with cranes mounted under the top hatch.

cargo_bay.description: The main central body of the submarine. It is a constant circular cross section. It is as l9ng as possible, subject to ballast tank volume needs at tje extreme foreward and aft ends of the sub.
cargo_bay.pressurization: The cargo bay is fully pressurizable and floodable, with water ports, pumps and valves at the bottom, and air ports, pumps and valves at the top. Partial flooding of the cargo bay is problematic for stability and control. Transient flooding is acceptable for very controlled loading/unloading operations at near zero speed and zero pitch and roll. Light payload operations are generally with the cargo bay fully flooded. Heavy payload operations are with the cargo bay generally dry. Whether dry or flooded, the cargo bay is generally operated at near ambient pressures to minimize structural loads

main_generator.description: One large generator. Rps input can be driven by small steam piston engine(s) or the standby diesel generator, one OR the other being clutched in through their own optimized gearboxes.

elect_gen_steam_engine.description: The normal operation source of electrical power generation. It is 'owned' by the electrical system and controller, not the powerplant system or controller. This is because it is closed loop controlled by the electrical system controller, based on a SteamAvailable flag from the powerplant controller. A variable flow rate valve is used for regulation.

diesel_engine.description: A medium diesel engine for standby power when surfaced. It is 'owned' by the electrical system controller. Intake and exhaust air are routed to an extendable snorkel, well above the waterline when surfaced. The fuel tank, adjacent to the engine, is refueled through a fluid connector next to the main personnel hatch. The coolant loop is plumbed directly to seawater ports at the bottom of the sub. a small battery with diode charger provide emergency start power

main_electric_bus.description: Actually an electric relay block, with A terminal connected to the battery, and B terminal connected to ALL electrical loads for now. I may create multiple power buses later.

external_power_connectors.description: Precise use cases are not certain, but the sub is generally expected to provide export power through electrical connectors all around the sub exterior. Although they are all nominally connected to the main bus, diodes may be used to charge the sub through dedicated charging ports, and to prevent the sub from draining power from external sources. Details of that TBD.

logic_overview: A guarded master electrical switch can be used to turn the main electrical bus on and off. This is effectively the ON/OFF switch for the sub.
The electrical system defaults to autonomous operation in the absence of operator guidance.

The system always wants a source of power besides the battery. Battery-only operation is considered an imminent emergency. There are three sources of power: reactor (steam), standby diesel, and shore power.

Autonomous power source selection: If the sub mode is anything other than Standby, the reactor is the preferred source of power. If ReactorSafeToRun is true, the electrical system controller will request the powerplant system to run the controller. The powerplant conyroller will run through a startup, ending either in SteamAvailable = true or ReactorSafeToRun = false. If SteamAvailable, the controller will clutch in the steam engine and regulate its operation. If ReactorSafeToRun is false, the steam engine is declutched, and the second preferred option is shore power. If ShorePowerAvailable, the ShorePower relay is closed, connecting shore power to the battery. If ShorePowerAvailable = false, the controller tries to run the diesel engine. If DieselEngineSafeToRun, the controller will initiate a startup ending in DieselEngineRunning = true, or DieselEngineSafeToRun = false. If DieselEngineRunning, the controller will clutch in the diesel engine and regulate it. If DieselEngineSafeToRun = false (snorkel submerged for example), an emergency is imminent. The operator is prompted to acknowledge the issue. If they do not acknowledge the issue within a few minutes, the controller will actively work to achieve Standby mode, to include EmergencySurface if appropriate.

supervisor.description: Supervisor is the top level controller managing the 'big picture' operation of the sub and most safety systems. It owns the SubState state machine, the 'Christmas tree' Dive Board, the environmental systems, flood detection and bilge pump systems, and fire detection and supression systems. It evaluates safety aspects of ballast and crane control systems.

SubState._meta: Entry_conditions must be met to enter that state from any other state. On_entry actions are triggered immediately upon state entry. Exit_conditions must be satisfied to leave that state for any other state. On_exit actions are triggered by leaving that state.

Surface.description: The sub has successfully surfaced surfaced, the cargo bay is fully flooded for light loads, fully empty for heavy loads. This is the default, home, and or safest state. The sub can be evacuated, and is in it's most stable surface condition. It is the only state the ship can be safely shutdown from.

Standby.description: The sub is surfaced and electrically functioning, but operation is not imminent, and the reactor is shut down.

Diving.description: The submarine's baseline and generally safest submerged state. Movement, UAA or DP, is unrestricted, hatches are closed, sealed, and disabled, cranes are stowed and disabled.

CraneReady.description: Speed is restricted low enough for total 6DOF motion with the bottom hatch open. Control is restricted to DP. The crane has taken up the onboard load, if there is any.

CraneDeployed.description: The bottom hatch is locked open, the crane is unrestricted and freely operating.

CraneLoading.description: the crane is actively taking up a load, actively controlling winch takeup, ballast reduction and stationkeeping until the load has been fully taken up and lifted a small distance.

CraneUnloading.description: The crane is actively unloading, controlling winch letout, ballast increase and stationkeeping until the load is fully released.

EmergencySurface.description: All ballast tanks blown, any crane load dropped, cargo bay possibly blown. In DP mode, the RCS is commanded max V_y. In UAA mode, max pitch and vertical velocity are commanded. At the surface, the autopilot may manage the breach, subsequent speed zeroing, hatch opening, and emergency beacon activation. Depends on the circumstances.
entry_conditions: To avoid multiple repetitions, EmergencySurface is a 'next_state' for all other states. You can never NOT EmergencySurface, even from Surface. You just never know.

control_loop_throttle_valve.description: Regulates transient and short term EngRPS with the main throttling valve. For rapid power reductions, a steam bypass valve can dump steam overboard to prevent an overpressure.

control_loop_feedwater_valve.description: Regulates steady state EngRPS with feedwater flow rate.

control_loop_coolant_valve.description: Regulates boiler temperature with reactor coolant flow rate.

control_loop_control_rods.description: Regulates the coolant temperature via a two loop cascade. The outer loop sets a reactivity setpoint to directly regulate the coolant temperature. The inner loop regulates reactivity with control rod position. Reactivity is measured as counts per second of a radiation detector (Geiger counter) placed above the fuel assembly in the RPV. When ReactorRunReq = 0 (SCRAM/shutdown) closed loop control is reset, and control rod position commanded to 0.0. For rapid, non-SCRAM power reductions, before reactivity can be brought down, reactor coolant is routed through a liquid/liquid heat exchanger to dump heat faster. For now, this logic will be included in the main coolant temp loops.

powerplant_supervisor_logic.description: Manages the status flags, modes, and other ancilliary non-loop aspects of the powerplant

ReactorRunReq.description: If ReactorRunReq AND ReactorSafeToRun then do the conditions_met actions. Else, do the conditions_not_met actions.
conditions_met: Allow the control loops to run each frame
Reactor coolant, feedwater, condenser coolant pumps on.
conditions_not_met: As various temperatures and pressures acheive steady state, turn off the relavent pumps, and close the steam bypass valve.

powerplant_supervisor_logic.feedwater_makeup: If the feedwater tank drops below a certain level, the desalinator is run until the proper level is reached. Bang-bang control.

FlightDisplay.description: This is a microcontroller that can output a HUD overlay directly to a cockpit player HUD, or overlay a gimballed camera view.
FlightDisplay.reference_sphere: Instead of a pitch ladder, a reference sphere of 'lattitude' and 'longitude' lines, centered at the origin of the player's or camera's POV provides primary attitude reference. Longitude lines indicate heading, latitude lines indicate pitch, and roll is implicit.
FlightDisplay.depth_tape: Vertical moving tape on right side of screen with numerical indication of current depth in the middle. 'Bugs' may indicate important depths, like current searfloor depth, surfaced depth, autopilot command depth, etc. An adjacent, smaller sub-bar indicate vertical velocity, with autopilot vertical velocity command, if active.
FlightDisplay.motion_cues: faint, distributed points that move to indicate self-motion.
FlightDisplay.target_self_spheres: For manual navigation and station keeping, a small target sphere and self sphere can be overlaid by maneuvering the sub. When the two spheres are exactly overlayed in position, size and heading, the sub is exactly at the desired position and orientation.
FlightDisplay.contact_diamonds: Contact diamonds are simply indicated positions with adjacent IDs for any positions or objects of interest. They may be waypoints, laser designated reference points, sonar contacts, transponders, beacons, other ships, subs, ROVs, crane hook position, anything.
FlightDisplay.speed_tape: Vertical moving tape on left side of screen indicating current and autopilot commanded velocity, if active.
FlightDisplay.heading_mcp_display: At the top center of the screen are numerical displays of commanded and actual headings. To the left and right of the heading indicators are multiple 'button boxes' indicating the inhibited, enabled, or activated status of many sub and autopilot modes. Examples include current state machine state (Surface, Diving, etc), top and bottom hatch status, crane deployment, DP/UAA, and TBD autopilot modes.

NavDisplay.description: A top-down moving map display. It can be selectively heading up or north up. It includes the game's map overlay, as well as any defined waypoints and moving contacts from many sources. It has a 'flight planning' submenu where a waypoint sequence can be created for nav display and autopilot guidance.

SynopticDisplay._meta: A reminder so I don't forget. Because you never know how things play out or what may happen, there should be an ability to query any parameter or constant in any Lua controller script, and if desired set that parameter to a new value. A log for all such changes should be recorded so that I can manually make these changes permanent in the Lua scripts. I will monitor and minimize the performance hit of this facility.
SynopticDisplay.description: This is the primary display for monitoring and control of shipwide systems. The 'home' page contents are TBD, but will include a textual list of all off-nominal indications. There will be dedicated pages for damage control, dive board, electrical system, environmental system, propulsion system, reactor maintenance, ballast system, crane operation, etc.
